key_management_model: KMIP Server and Client SDKs; HSM-backed (embedded by HSM vendors); QKD-integrated key management
architecture_type: Pure-code SDKs; KMIP-based key management fabric
primary_platforms: HSMs, cloud, storage, mobile, automotive, IoT, embedded systems
target_industries: Storage, security, cloud, automotive, IoT, Enterprise
pqc_roadmap_details: KMIP v3.0 and PKCS#11 v3.2 are coming soon as the first PQC-ready releases of each standard.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: QKD clients retrieve keys from any ETSI-compliant KME — ETSI 014, 004 and SKIP, with ETSI 020 coming soon.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Tiny Embedded & IoT SDKs available; supports automotive and IoT endpoints.

product_brief: A Python library providing cryptographic recipes and primitives, including support for X.509 certificates, KEM, and PQC algorithms via OpenSSL, AWS-LC, and BoringSSL.
pqc_capability_description: Supports ML-KEM key encapsulation and ML-DSA signing/verification. Available when using OpenSSL 3.5.0+, AWS-LC, or BoringSSL. Includes support for X.509 certificates with ML-DSA keys, external mu support for ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and HPKE (RFC 9180).
crypto_primitives: ECDSA, DSA, RSA, Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, X448, DH, ChaCha20, AES, AES-CCM, AES-GCM, AES-GCM-SIV, AES-OCB3, AES-SIV, TripleDES, Camellia, Argon2, HKDF, PBKDF2, Scrypt, ML-KEM, ML-DSA
pqc_roadmap_details: PQC algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) are available in version 47.0.0+ with AWS-LC/BoringSSL and version 48.0.0+ with OpenSSL 3.5.0+. Version 49.0.0 adds X.509 support for ML-DSA and external mu support.
signature_schemes: ECDSA, DSA, RSA (PKCS1v15, PSS), Ed25519, Ed448, ML-DSA
implementation_attack_surface: Fixed buffer overflow issue with non-contiguous buffers (CVE-2026-39892). Fixed private key leakage on binary elliptic curves (CVE-2026-26007). Rejects incorrectly encoded EC private keys to ensure constant-time processing.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Fixed cross-compilation of CFFI bindings for embedded systems.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Multiple backwards incompatible changes in recent versions (removal of x86_64 macOS, 32-bit Windows, Python 3.8, binary curves, OpenSSL 1.1.x). Requires migration to 64-bit Python and updated OS/architectures.
